entries.descriptionOriginal: CSStats Training Map Subscribe today to access: Warmup has 3 options: Range: Bots standing still, provides 3 range settings. Rush: Bots run at you from behind cover, this mode has a streak counter and the ability to adjust the amount of bots that spawn. When a bot reaches the platform your streak ends and the bots are reset back to the boxes. Shuffle: The bots shuffle to mimic sideways movement and boxes and cover are also placed on the map. Aim Challenges: Time Trial has 3 difficulty settings; Open, Advanced and Pro, with Pro being the most difficult of the 3. Bots will spawn in front of you and disappear quickly, the map will track how many of the bots you successfully killed out of the 45 bots that will spawn. This is a great benchmark to see how you match up against the Pros and your friends. The worlds best CS:GO players average around 42 out of 45 on the Pro setting. Speed Challenge is all about how fast you can kill 50 bots, tracking your time and KPM. Prefire Challenges: Prefire puts you on real maps in real scenarios and you have to kill the bots, it will track your time and attempts. Use this as a good way to get warmed up peaking spots on real maps and track your performance to see if your times are improving. Movement has 3 modes: KZ: Practice your jumping and air strafing movement on our KZ map Bhop: Bunny hop is a good way to practice air strafing and fast movement. Surf: Surfing is a fun movement in CS:GO, not very useful in competitive though. Spraying Practice: Practice your Spraying skills with new mode where you can see your stats of previous spraydowns. About csstats.gg csstats.gg lets you track your matches and stats across Valve’s matchmaking, as well as Faceit and ESEA. You also receive advanced statistics and can track when cheaters in your matches are banned! Match History An overview of your past matches. Map Stats: See what maps you play the most, and where you have the highest win rate! Sign up and start tracking your matches here. entries.descriptionOriginal: New Update 2026/10/14 Thanks to everyone who shared feedback regarding the map. Rather than just fix the many broken parts of this map, I've redesigned and rebuilt the entire map from scratch. The overall scale and dimensions of the playable space, and map spawnpoint positions have been kept the same in the rebuild, so the map should feel and play the same. It took a while because I wanted to make sure that everything was sound and that it was deserving of a rebuild, but this is admittedly the reason why the previous version remained practically unplayable for several weeks. Along with the rebuild, many features have been improved, fixed, or are new with this update: Modes: Flick: horizontal flicks, 30 kills, 3 difficulties. Rush: bots rush towards you, game resets if they reach you. Speed: replaces 100k mode which was broken beyond belief, same concept. All modes track your best scores in between sessions. Main Changes / Fixes: Fixed all of the previous longstanding bugs by deleting everything and starting again. Added option to select default / random bot models. Knife menu fixed. Bot strafe massively improved. Bots now move independently of one another instead of all in the same direction. Additionally, bots that are moving whilst jumping will no longer fly across the map (this is an engine bug but I've tried to ensure it never occurs). Bot Shadows can be turned off which may give a slight performance boost. Chat Commands: !lock: toggles the menu between locked/unlocked. !restart restarts the entire map as if you were joining for the first time. WIP: Outstanding features that were in the previous version of the map but are no longer present include Peek walls, Elevation, and Uneven Ground. They will be added in a future update. Please let me know if you have any suggestions or notice anything wrong with the map. If the map doesn't update on its own, try unsubscribing and then subscribing to the map again. game_alias custom;map_workshop 3077265396 cs2aim_testbed

entries.descriptionOriginal: Details A benchmark for testing CS2 performance and FPS, it simulates typical things that would happen during a usual round like bomb plants, nade throws, gunfire, smoke spams, etc... Interpreting Results Example >> FPS: Avg=517.3, P1=183.5 Average FPS over the entire run P1 > 1% lows, the slowest 1% of frames, basically the lowest your FPS got over the whole run. The results from this benchmark shouldn't be compared against real competitive matches, due to your client having to simulate the entire game, which doesn't happen when playing on a server. This benchmark is 100% reliable and reproducible and as such should only be used to compare results against ITSELF, to check for config/hardware changes. Have fun and enjoy! entries.descriptionOriginal: Changelog: - fixed scripting after new script system Mirage EGO PEEK Trainer – Because Holding Angles is for Cowards Is your team mad at you for dying in mid again? Are they spamming “?” in chat while you confidently type “timing” in all caps? Do your teammates beg you to stop dry-peeking Window, only for you to wide swing into an AWP anyway? Is your ego fragile? Fear not—because with the Mirage EGO Peek Trainer, you will never lose a duel in mid ever again! What is this map? This isn’t your average aim trainer. This is a mid-fight simulator designed to make you an absolute demon in Mirage mid. You will peek, you will duel, and you will develop the muscle memory to win every single fight—assuming your aim is halfway decent. Key Features: Instant mid duels: No more waiting for eco rounds or your team to throw. Just fight. Over and over. Varied enemy spawns: Because let’s be real, fighting the same angle gets boring. No utility, no excuses: Smokes? Flashes? Please. If you’re not winning dry peeks, are you even peeking correctly? Pure ego peeking simulation: If you die, it’s because you hesitated. Or you just whiffed. Either way, skill issue. Perfect warm-up tool: Play a few rounds here before matchmaking, and suddenly, you’re the main character in your games. Available Scenarios Here are the different scenarios you will face while using the Mirage EGO Peek Trainer. Each one is designed to replicate the most common fights in Mirage Mid, making sure you’re always ready to swing, shoot, and survive. Mid Left: The bot will peek you from the left side of Window. A classic fight—just don’t whiff. Mid Right: The bot will peek you from the right side of Window. If you lose this, uninstall. Mid Jump: The bot will jump from Window to Underpass. Ever wanted to farm free frags? Now’s your chance. Mid Connector: The bot will peek you from Connector. Because there’s always some lurking rat waiting there. Mid Short: The bot will peek you from Catwalk. If you’re not pre-aiming this, you’re already dead. Mid Rush: The bot will full-send down Mid. Survive the stampede or get trampled. Double Mid: Multiple bots will spawn at once. A true ego-check—are you built different? Connect With Me Want more maps, updates, or just a place to discuss how to perfect the art of ego peeking? Join the community! Twitter/X: x.com/drippycatcs Discord: discord.gg/X2tEsZDYDE So load in, stop baiting, and start taking every fight like it’s match point in a Major final—because real ones never prefire, they pre-believe. How to Start the Map While Queuing Want to warm up while waiting for a match? entries.descriptionOriginal: Map made by Panzer, ported by GumPum. Use "High" on shader, textures and particles in video settings or some parts might look bad. Compared to the original CSS version some changes have been made which got either approved or wished directly by the original creator. Changes: ● Added water splashes on ground and water ripples on water in the rain area. ● Added reflections to ice and bhop stones in the rain area. ● Made the pit before the first grass tube deeper (doesn't effect gameplay). ● Replaced invisible walls in the canal level with a visible one. ● Removed invisible walls in the grass level. ● Removed teleporter on top of the first stone in the neon end room. ● Reduced speed of some booster. ● Removed trail deagles, moved last deagle and fire scout into weapons room and removed boost from scout. Unlock all secret buttons to get access to the weapons room. ● Removed doors from every stage. ● Added non solid chicken which bhop around in the spawn area. Reasons: ● Water splash and ripples, reflections and deeper pit looks better. ● Replaced invisible walls in the canal level with a visible wall so people don't get stopped out of nowhere. ● Removed the invisible walls in the grass level because they are useless, only preventing players from doing very tiny shortcuts. Also making these walls visible would look bad. ● Removed the teleporter at the first stone in the neon end room because that one was not always working in the original css version and some top speedrunner already using it for a shortcut. Some people were sad when I made that teleporter always work in my csgo port, so I think it's better to remove it completely to make the shortcut possible consistantly. ● Reduced speed of some booster because the map was made for scroll and now most people are using autojump for which the booster were to strong. ● Removed boost effect on fire scout for competetive reasons. With most server using a timer plugin, people can just teleport or noclip to the endzone grabbing the final trail deagle. Decided to not throw the secret buttons away and giving them still a purpose by being necessary to get into the weapons room. ● Removed doors in every stage because they aren't needed when using a timer plugin where people can teleport everywhere. Also it was possible to touch them by accident and ruining a run. ● I added bhopping chicken because ( ͡~ ͜ʖ ͡°). Known issues: ● A few lighting issues on minor spots. ● Upper level are visible in reflections sometimes. ● Can get stuck on slopes (i suspect it's a cs2 problem and not the maps problem). ● Slide areas not optimal, have to wait for valve to add script support to make it properly. ● Texture in neon level on the tubes and below the circles looks weird. If you have any questions you can leave a comment and i will be happy to give an answer.

entries.descriptionOriginal: Info A new take on the classic Prophunt gamemode, now possible in CS2 thanks to cs_script! Now you too can hide as various props and annoy seekers using custom taunts recorded by Jacky Your prop will try to perfectly align to the ground to make it harder for seekers to find you. Gamerules Props Props spawn as a random object from the map and get 60 seconds to hide before the seekers are released Your health depends on the size of your prop: small props have 25 HP, medium 50 and big 100 Props can reroll into a different prop a few times per life Props are forced to taunt every minute Every prop is rerolled in the middle of the round, seekers are blinded while props hide again Props get one flashbang per life and another right before the prop switch Props that get found are out for the round and watch their living teammates Props win if anyone is still alive when time runs out, or if every seeker leaves Seekers About 30% of players start as seekers, last round's seekers are picked last While waiting to be released, seekers have the info menu open on the Deploy tab Seekers are released with an M4A1-S and respawn when they die, after waiting 30 seconds Every shot or knife swing that hits nothing costs the seeker health, so don't spray at everything A random seeker gets a wallhack grenade with 2 minutes left and again with 1 minute left, it outlines every prop close to where it lands Players joining mid round join the seekers Controls Props Freeze prop: , or stand still for 3 seconds. entries.descriptionOriginal: English When the map is loaded, the current version number will be displayed in the in-game text panel. If the displayed version is lower than v2.2.1, or no version number is shown, please update the map to ensure the best experience. This map is a modified version of the classic Aim Rush warm-up and aim training map created by JoeyyBiden$$. Aim Rush has always been one of my favorite warm-up maps, so I decided to build upon the original version by adding several features and improvements that I personally wanted to use. Original Creator: JoeyyBiden$$ Original Workshop Item: Main Changes Added support for 20 different knife types, with automatic knife replacement. Expanded the weapon selection with P2000, CZ75-Auto, PP-Bizon, AUG, SG 553, G3SG1, SCAR-20, Nova, XM1014, MAG-7, Sawed-Off, M249, and Negev. Added three Enhanced Bot behavior modes with different difficulty levels. Added a separate Bot Target Tracking option for the three Enhanced Bot modes. This setting only affects Enhanced Bots. Fixed an issue where weapon skins were not displayed on the CT side. Added selectable Zeus, Smoke Grenade, Flashbang, HE Grenade, Molotov / Incendiary Grenade, and Decoy Grenade. Added separate Limited Utility and Infinite Utility modes. Added a separate option to enable or disable Bot attacks. Added a Headshot-Only Damage mode. Reworked the pistol mode and weapon selection logic. Fixed an issue where pistols could not be automatically replaced while using pistol mode. Added automatic configuration saving. Your configuration is automatically saved whenever you enter the map. Usage Guide & Feedback For detailed usage instructions, preset configurations, Bot logic, and other information, please visit the GitHub repository: Aim Rush - Community Modified Version | GitHub If you encounter any bugs, have questions about the map, or would like to suggest a feature, you can open an issue on GitHub. This makes it easier for me to review, organize, and follow up on reported problems: Report an Issue / Ask a Question Credits & Permission This project has not received official permission from the original creator. I do not claim ownership of the original map or any of its original assets. All rights to the original map and its content belong to the original creator. I have attempted to contact the original creator through Steam and other available methods, but I have not received a response so far. Players are divided into teams and start to pull the rope at speed, so as not to be at the bottom. "Rock paper scissors" "The Glass Tile Game" is a small bridge consisting of ordinary and tempered glass. Jumping over the tempered glass will lead you straight to victory while the regular glass will be your ticket to the other side. After the remaining players reach the edge of the bridge, here is the final stage called "Not a Squid Game" comes. Players get knives and have a melee fight where only one winner will emerge. entries.descriptionOriginal: Info A new take on the classic Prophunt gamemode, now possible in CS2 thanks to cs_script! Now you too can hide as various props and annoy seekers using custom taunts recorded by Jacky Your prop will try to perfectly align to the ground to make it harder for seekers to find you. Gamerules Props Props spawn as a random object from the map and get 60 seconds to hide before the seekers are released Your health depends on the size of your prop: small props have 25 HP, medium 50 and big 100 Props can reroll into a different prop a few times per life Props are forced to taunt every minute Every prop is rerolled in the middle of the round, seekers are blinded while props hide again Props get one flashbang per life and another right before the prop switch Props that get found are out for the round and watch their living teammates Props win if anyone is still alive when time runs out, or if every seeker leaves Seekers About 30% of players start as seekers, last round's seekers are picked last While waiting to be released, seekers have the info menu open on the Deploy tab Seekers are released with an M4A1-S and respawn when they die, after waiting 30 seconds Every shot or knife swing that hits nothing costs the seeker health, so don't spray at everything A random seeker gets a wallhack grenade with 2 minutes left and again with 1 minute left, it outlines every prop close to where it lands Players joining mid round join the seekers Controls Props Freeze prop: , or stand still for 3 seconds. Press again or move to unfreeze Slide a frozen prop: hold and use Turn a frozen prop: hold and move the mouse, tips it over Finer sliding and turning: also hold Sneak past a door without opening it: hold Reroll prop: , or type !r or !reroll in chat Flashbang: Taunt: Leave a decoy clone of your prop: Everyone Show info menu: type !i or !info in chat Game Settings The lobby host can change the game settings from the Settings tab of the info menu, most of them apply without a round restart. You can also type !config in chat, on a dedicated server use say !config in the server console instead. entries.introZh: 通过多组瞄准测试比较速度与准确度，逐次记录结果，帮助玩家寻找适合自己的鼠标灵敏度。
entries.descriptionOriginal: Find the mouse sensitivity that fits YOUR aim — measured, not guessed. The map tests your aim at several sensitivities and recommends the one where you are fastest and most precise. Every run makes the result tighter: your saved runs are combined, and the next run measures around the current best estimate. What you do (about 10 minutes) Type your sensitivity and mouse DPI in chat once: !sens 1.66 !dpi 800 (the map cannot read your settings; it remembers them). Range of motion: swing left and right — the room's light lines and the scale on the wall turn green as far as you turn. Eyes closed: turn 90° right / left and shoot to finish (5 each). This gives the sensitivity that matches your feel; unless it is close to another value, block 5 of the aim board tests it, and the result compares it with your best. At the same sensitivity as your last run, this step and the range of motion are reused (type !full to redo them). Six blocks at different sensitivities (your centre, ×1.35 and ÷1.35, then two values chosen from your results or the one that matches your feel, then the centre again). Each block: 6 warm-up and 36 scored targets on an aim board (singles and three at once, in three sizes down to a head, in new places every block; misses are counted) and 4 wall peeks with the AK-47 against a bot. When a block asks for another value, type sensitivity X in the console and shoot NEXT. Forgot to change it? Type !redo to play the block again. Result: your recommended sensitivity, combined over all your saved runs, with its likely range, how much a single run moves, the range within 3% of your best, eDPI and cm/360. Good to know One run alone pins your sensitivity down to about ±10–15%, so its own number moves from run to run. Use the combined value at the top of the result screen: it moves less with every run. Changed your resolution or aspect ratio (e.g. to 4:3 stretched)? Start fresh: type !clear, then !clear yes. A new DPI or m_yaw is taken into account by itself (type !dpi / !yaw). How it decides Aim board: throughput (ISO 9241-9) on the time from your first movement until the target is hit (follow-up shots after a miss included, your reaction time left out) per sensitivity, so fast flickers and careful aimers are both judged by how fast they really land the hit, with your accuracy measured over all shots in units of the target size; peak of a curve fitted over the tested values, each weighted by how precisely it was measured. The recommendation stays inside the values you tested. Wall peeks: how fast your first shot comes after the enemy becomes visible and how close to the head it lands (a throughput like the aim board's, with the head as the target); they count at most as much as the aim board. Blind 90° turns: the sensitivity that matches your feel is tested, not trusted — your current value may feel best without being what your hand turns by. Performance is usually flat over a wide range of sensitivities, so the result also shows every value within 3% of your best. Blocks 4 and 5 are chosen from your results so far and never repeat a tested value; block 6 repeats block 1 to measure practice or fatigue. Earlier runs are combined with a random-effects model; a run that disagrees is down-weighted, never trusted blindly. Tracking practice Shoot TRACKING on the start screen to try a new sensitivity on a moving target: no shooting, just keep your crosshair on the yellow ball. Each 10-second round shows your on-target rate on a small display and on a red / yellow / green gauge under the board, and the display keeps your average per sensitivity. It is practice only — not part of the measurement. Flick practice Shoot FLICK (left of NEXT) to practise flicks, then START (lower left) to begin: 100 light-blue balls the size of a head (the CS2 head hitbox) appear one at a time, the next the moment you hit one. Most flicks are micro flicks, fewer are mid-range and long ones; half go to the left and half to the right, in no fixed order. At the end you get your time, accuracy, first-shot hits, how far your first shots land (in ball radii, too far or short), and the same per distance and per direction. Your last 5 rounds are shown on the wall on your left with the sensitivity, DPI and m_yaw they were played with, and the wall on your right charts where each first shot landed on the ball, flicks to the left and to the right side by side. During a round the lower left button becomes CANCEL (stops the round, nothing is recorded) and BACK works too; afterwards shoot RETRY to go again. It is practice only — not part of the measurement. How to use and every command are also on the wall to your right in the start room. Chat commands: !sens !dpi !yaw (your m_yaw if not 0.022, e.g. 0.0165 for 4:3 stretched) !lang en|ru|ja|zh|ko !restart !result (your result as text in the console, to copy and share) !full (measure the range and eyes-closed turns again) !redo (play the current block again) !clear, then !clear yes (delete saved results) Languages: English, Русский, 日本語, 中文, 한국어. Works with any m_yaw: if yours is not 0.022 (e.g. 0.0165 for 4:3 stretched), type !yaw once so cm/360 is right. Contact: questions, bug reports and requests by DM on X: @sKplZifv2
